method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Stocks rise as SpaceX makes market debut; oil slides on Gulf peace hopes
Equities.reason: Major market-regime move: SpaceX's record IPO acted as a large risk-on catalyst while reported US‑Iran ceasefire/Strait of Hormuz reopening lowered oil risk premium — supportive for broad equities and cyclicals.

Equities.title: SpaceX market cap tops $2 trillion after shares of Elon Musk's rocket company gain 19% on debut
Equities.summary: SpaceX shares soared on Friday as trading commenced on the Nasdaq.
Equities.reason: Systemic single‑name event: historic, oversubscribed IPO and large first‑day pop concentrated investor demand and created a new market-cap heavyweight — supportive for risk appetite and tech/AI leadership theme.

Equities.title: Space stocks slump as blistering rally cools after SpaceX market debut
Equities.reason: Important micro-to-macro transmission: profit-taking and rotation away from speculative ‘proxy’ names after the big IPO introduce a localized pullback risk within the tech/space cohort, mildly negative for that sector.

Equities.title: Anthropic suspends latest AI models after US blocks access to foreigners
Equities.summary: Trump administration directs company to limit access to foreign nationals on national security grounds
Equities.reason: Regulatory/national‑security shock to AI leadership: US export-control action and restricted model access are a clear negative for AI platform growth narratives and could temper sector multiple expansion.

Equities.title: Global equity funds draw third weekly inflow as investors buy the dip
Equities.reason: Fund flows confirm broad risk appetite: continued inflows into global equity funds reinforce the market-wide risk‑on move and underpin liquidity for equities.

Equities.title: Paramount-WBD merger wins approval from DOJ
Equities.summary: The DOJ approval is an important milestone for the roughly $110 billion deal, though it could still face legal challenges from state attorneys general.
Equities.reason: M&A positive for media/market sentiment: DOJ clearance reduces regulatory overhang on a large deal and is a modest positive for merger-driven equity returns and risk appetite.

Equities.title: Why an Iran deal might not be dovish for the Fed
Equities.reason: Macro nuance/counter-signal: while a peace deal reduces geopolitical risk, the article flags that lower oil/ozone risk may not materially ease inflation or Fed policy — a mild restraint on sustained risk‑on positioning.

Rates.title: Bank of England: Hold stance extended as inflation risks linger – TD Securities
Rates.summary: TD Securities economists expect the Bank of England (BoE) to keep Bank Rate at 3.75% with a 7-2 vote as Greene joins Pill in calling for a hike. They highlight persistent inflation pressures, upside risks from energy and airfare, and softer demand.
Rates.reason: TD note emphasizes persistent inflation upside and split vote at the BoE — supports a higher-for-longer UK rates narrative and potential bond selloff. High relevance given proximity to a BoE decision and explicit rate-vote commentary.

Rates.title: BoE expected to hold rates as economists split on next move – Reuters poll
Rates.summary: A Reuters poll released on Friday found that the Bank of England (BoE) is projected to keep the Bank Rate at 3.75% at the June 18 meeting, based on a survey of 65 economists.
Rates.reason: Poll consensus of a hold combined with economists split on next move reinforces uncertainty and the possibility that sticky inflation keeps rates elevated — modestly negative for UK bond prices ahead of the meeting.

Rates.title: United Kingdom: Growth resilience but softer inflation – Deutsche Bank
Rates.summary: Deutsche Bank’s Sanjay Raja says the UK economy is tracking close to the Bank of England’s Scenario A, with stronger‑than‑expected early‑2026 GDP but a cooling labour market and easing price pressures.
Rates.reason: Softer price pressures and a cooling labour market point to eventual easing of BoE tightness — mildly supportive for UK bonds (lower yields) even as growth resilience tempers the move.

Rates.title: Federal Reserve: Warsh policy shift and inflation focus – NBC
Rates.summary: National Bank of Canada (NBC) strategists assess how Kevin Warsh may reshape Federal Reserve (Fed) policy.
Rates.reason: Assessment that Kevin Warsh may shift Fed policy toward a stronger inflation focus implies higher-for-longer US rates and steeper US yield path — material negative for bond prices and market liquidity; high relevance given Fed leadership change.

Rates.title: How to tame the inflation python
Rates.summary: A ‘wait and see’ monetary policy strategy risks repeating the mistakes made in 2008
Rates.reason: FT argues against a passive 'wait-and-see' stance, implying policymakers may need firmer action to contain inflation — supports a hawkish tilt and higher-for-longer rates narrative, moderately negative for bonds.

Rates.title: Social Security COLA for 2027 may jump to 4.7%, one estimate finds. This chart shows prices driving the increase
Rates.summary: As inflation climbs, Social Security beneficiaries may see a higher cost-of-living adjustment in 2027. Here's which costs spiked most over the past 12 months.
Rates.reason: Higher COLA estimates signal more persistent underlying inflation pressures in the US, which would keep Fed policy tighter for longer and be negative for US Treasury prices.

FX.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: Fed, BoJ, BoE and RBA decisions take center stage
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY) lost ground during the week, down 0.27% to trade near the 99.80 level as investors prepared for a heavy central bank calendar the following week.
FX.reason: Dollar softening highlighted ahead of a heavy central bank week; meaningful for FX flows as rate decisions can drive USD direction. Signals mild USD weakness into meetings.

FX.title: Japanese Yen holds as traders switch focus to BoJ hike and Warsh’s first Fed meeting
FX.summary: The USD/JPY pair trades near the 160.20 region on Friday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains slightly under pressure, while investors prepare for a key central bank week featuring the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) policy decision and Kevin Warsh’s first Federal Reserve
FX.reason: USD/JPY elevated and JPY under pressure ahead of BoJ hike and Fed leadership change — a central-bank-driven, high-relevance USD/JPY narrative implying USD strength (negative for non-USD FX).

FX.title: US Dollar: Peace deal talk keeps support intact – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Chris Turner notes that a potential US-Iran peace deal has softened the Dollar, but DXY is still holding firm. He highlights that energy supply losses and inflation risks persist unless Oil flows freely through the Strait of Hormuz.
FX.reason: Geopolitical peace-talks are putting some downside on the USD, but ING flags lingering energy/inflation risks that keep DXY supported — overall a mild USD-softening but with offsetting risks.

FX.title: New Zealand Dollar dips as robust US sentiment, inflation data underpin US Dollar
FX.summary: NZD/USD trades around 0.5830 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.15% on the day as the US Dollar (USD) maintains a firm tone following a series of strong US economic releases.
FX.reason: Firm US data underpinning USD leads to NZD weakness vs USD. Relevant as a near-term USD-support datapoint; technical/short-term move so moderate relevance.

FX.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish forecasts point to higher terminal rate – Nomura
FX.summary: Nomura’s European Economics team, led by Andrzej Szczepaniak and colleagues, notes that the ECB delivered a 25bp hike to a 2.25% depo rate and unveiled more hawkish forecasts.
FX.reason: ECB hiking and more-hawkish forecasts are a clear EUR-supportive, central-bank-led narrative — significant for EUR crosses and EUR/USD given rate-differential implications.

FX.title: British Pound: Poised to fall toward 1.3100 against US Dollar – BBH
FX.summary: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad says GBP/USD has given back part of its US-Iran-related gains and is expected to fall to 1.3100 as United States (US) growth outpaces the United Kingdom (UK).
FX.reason: House view that GBP will weaken vs USD as US outpaces UK — a bank FX forecast tied to macro differentials. Single-bank note, so moderate relevance.

FX.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: RSI enters overbought territory as bears defend 1.4000
FX.summary: USD/CAD trades on the front foot on Friday as lower Oil prices weigh on the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) amid cautious optimism that the United States (US) and Iran could reach an agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
FX.reason: USD/CAD technical/price-forecast piece where oil-driven CAD weakness supports USD/CAD. Classified as technical so relevance capped; signals USD strength vs CAD.

FX.title: CEE FX: Risk-on bounce but policy still key – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky notes that headlines on a possible end to the US-Iran conflict triggered a risk-on move, helping Central and Eastern European currencies erase recent losses.
FX.reason: Risk-on move from peace-talk headlines has supported CEE FX — relevant as a regional EM/FX flow note tied to lower USD safe-haven demand, but policy considerations still matter.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness raises intervention concerns – Scotiabank
FX.summary: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/JPY is steady but elevated, with recent gains already surpassing prior intervention-trigger levels. A 25 bps Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike on Tuesday is widely anticipated, and markets price nearly on
FX.reason: Intervention risk is high-impact for FX; USD/JPY surpassing prior intervention thresholds combined with imminent BoJ move makes this a high-relevance USD/JPY/JPY story — implies USD strength (negative for non-USD).

FX.title: Euro holds steady against the US Dollar as markets await clarity on a possible US-Iran peace deal
FX.summary: EUR/USD fluctuates between modest gains and losses heading into the weekend as traders await Tehran's decision on a possible agreement with the United States (US) to end the war in the Middle East. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1573 and is o
FX.reason: Peace-deal uncertainty is a direct USD-driver; here EUR/USD holding with upside tied to potential USD softening. Relevant near-term geopolitical FX flow note.

FX.title: Canadian Dollar: Overbought Dollar holds near 1.40 ceiling – Scotiabank
FX.summary: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret observe that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is weighed down by weaker Oil prices linked to Iran peace hopes, even as improved risk appetite offers some support.
FX.reason: Oil-linked CAD weakness amid Iran peace optimism is a clear commodity-currency FX story; important for USD/CAD and risk-sensitive CAD flows.

FX.title: Indian Rupee: External shocks pressure currency outlook – Commerzbank
FX.summary: Commerzbank analysts Charlie Lay and Moses Lim argue that the Rupee remains vulnerable to external shocks, notably Middle East tensions, higher energy costs and El Nino-related risks.
FX.reason: External shocks (energy, Middle East) leave INR vulnerable — relevant EMFX vulnerability note tied to USD/energy-driven flows, but not a first-order global FX regime shift.

FX.title: British Pound stalls as UK GDP shrinks, diplomacy boosts risk mood
FX.summary: The Pound Sterling (GBP) turns negative against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday after UK data showed the economy contracted in April, while rising prospects of an agreement between the US and Iran improved risk appetite.
FX.reason: Domestic UK GDP contraction is a material negative for GBP versus USD; combined with risk-on from diplomacy, the data-driven GBP weakness is a meaningful FX driver.

FX.title: US officials' comments on Iran negotiations put mild pressure on US Dollar
FX.summary: United States Vice President JD Vance said on Friday that Iran would not receive cash or released funds simply for signing a potential agreement, pushing back against what he described as false information surrounding a possible deal to reopen the Strait of Ho
FX.reason: Official US comments that complicate a peace deal are nudging USD slightly lower; relevant as near-term geopolitical messaging that affects USD flows.

FX.title: Euro supported by hawkish ECB rhetoric as British Pound struggles after weak GDP
FX.summary: EUR/GBP holds firm on Friday, with the Euro (EUR) modestly outperforming the British Pound (GBP) as weak UK Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data reinforced signs of a slowing economy. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 0.8633, up from an intraday low
FX.reason: ECB hawkishness vs UK economic weakness creates a clear EUR/GBP narrative; central-bank/data divergence justifies inclusion despite being a non-USD cross.

FX.title: South Korean Won: Authorities step up FX stabilisation push – Societe Generale
FX.summary: Societe Generale highlights that South Korean authorities have launched a multi-pronged FX stabilisation package to address short-term USD funding stress and speculative pressures on the Korean Won.
FX.reason: Active policy measures to stabilise KRW and address USD funding stress are high-relevance FX intervention/funding-news — supportive for KRW and important for EM FX funding dynamics.

FX.title: Breaking: United States Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index rises to 48.9 in June
FX.summary: Consumer confidence in the United States (US) improved slightly in June, with the University of Michigan's (UoM) Consumer Sentiment Index rising to 48.9 in the flash estimate from 44.8 in May. This print came in better than the market expectation of 46.
FX.reason: Improved US consumer sentiment is a modest USD-support datapoint; relevant to FX as it feeds into USD bias alongside other US data.

Commodities.reason: Silver is reacting to USD moves and shifting safe‑haven flows rather than fundamental supply shocks. USD weakness provides some upside; move is modest and FX/flow transmission is the primary driver, so relevance is medium‑low.

Commodities.reason: An increase in working gas storage capacity is a supply/midstream-side augmentation that dampens seasonal tightness and price spikes risk. This is a direct, fundamentals-driven supply signal for natural gas, hence clear negative tilt with straightforward relevance.

Commodities.reason: This is a technical/price‑forecast piece (RSI/SMA signal) suggesting near‑term downside bias for WTI. Technical articles have capped relevance per guidelines; signals are short‑term and lower relevance to structural commodity narrative.

Commodities.reason: Regulatory scrutiny that could constrain a 24/7 oil contract affects market structure and liquidity for crude futures. Commodities.title: Despite US Help, Little Oil Has Gone Through Strait of Hormuz
Commodities.reason: Continued constraints on shipments through the Strait of Hormuz implies persistent physical flow disruption and an oil risk premium. This is a direct supply‑flow issue for crude with above‑average relevance and a clear bullish impact on oil prices.

Commodities.title: Investment firms join Donald Trump’s $100bn race for Venezuelan oil
Commodities.summary: Lionheart Capital and Keo Energy create Nasdaq-listed company to pursue assets in Latin American nation.
Commodities.reason: Private‑sector push into Venezuelan oil assets suggests potential medium‑term supply upside if investment and exports scale—a modest bearish structural signal for crude. Impact is longer‑term and uncertain, so relevance is moderate.

Crypto.title: VanEck bets BNB’s real-world usage can stand out in a crowded crypto ETF market
Crypto.reason: Signals continued institutional product innovation and differentiation within crypto ETFs/ETP space. Positive for BNB adoption narratives and alt-ETF issuance, but limited market-wide impact compared with Bitcoin ETF developments.

Crypto.title: Bloomberg Analyst: Most Bitcoin ETF Investors Have Stayed Put Despite Outflows
Crypto.reason: Reinforces ETF investor resilience and stickiness of institutional flows into Bitcoin products — supportive for market liquidity and demand for BTC-related financial products.

Crypto.title: Metaplanet buys Siiibo Securities to accelerate bitcoin financial ecosystem plans
Crypto.reason: Corporate acquisition aimed at expanding bitcoin financial services signals further institutionalization and product development in the BTC ecosystem — positive structural adoption news.

Crypto.title: BlackRock files to list its bitcoin income ETF, with expected debut next week
Crypto.reason: Major asset manager filing for a bitcoin income ETF is a high‑profile expansion of institutional product suite — materially bullish for structural demand and legitimization of crypto financial products.

Crypto.title: Kalshi’s crypto perpetuals spark debate over whether they’re futures or swaps
Crypto.reason: Regulatory uncertainty over novel derivatives raises legal/compliance risk for crypto market structure and could restrict product expansion — negative for liquidity and institutional uptake.

Crypto.title: FTX's Sam Bankman-Fried loses appeal of criminal conviction on fraud, conspiracy charges
Crypto.reason: High‑profile legal development sustains negative regulatory and reputational backdrop for the industry, potentially keeping oversight intensity and compliance costs elevated.

Crypto.title: Monero price rockets 33% to $438 amid $120 million onchain laundering maze
Crypto.reason: Large illicit flows through a privacy coin and subsequent freezing actions heighten AML/regulatory scrutiny and counterparty risk in crypto markets — negative for privacy-coin sentiment and regulatory outlook.

Crypto.title: Ripple wants AI agents to pay in XRP and RLUSD. The market is still mostly USDC
Crypto.reason: Product and payments innovation linking crypto to AI agent payments is a constructive adoption narrative for XRP/RLUSD, but USDC dominance tempers near-term market impact.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin steadies above $63,000 as its worst week in months got a late macro rescue
Crypto.reason: Short‑term price stabilization on macro flow support is mildly positive for market sentiment and liquidations risk, but this is primarily a technical/macro-driven price story with limited structural implications.

Crypto.title: Top cryptographers can't agree on Bitcoin's biggest quantum question
Crypto.reason: Ongoing debate about quantum threats to Bitcoin introduces a longer‑term security uncertainty. Important conceptually but limited immediate market transmission.
